description: The line plot illustrates the Attack Success Rate (ASR) across eight different target labels — “cf”, “bb”, “WNBA”, “ESPN”, “NHL”, “FIFA”, “Estadio”, and “athletics” — under a clean-label poisoning attack with a poison rate of 10% (2.5% of total data), as reported in the paper “Efficient Trigger Word Insertion”. The x-axis is categorical, listing the target labels in order from left to right, while the y-axis is linear, ranging from 0.5 to 0.95 with tick marks at intervals of 0.05, labeled “ASR”. Three strategies are compared: “start” (solid green line with circle markers), “random” (solid orange line with cross markers), and “end” (solid purple line with circle markers). The “start” strategy begins at ASR ≈ 0.77 for “cf”, drops sharply to ≈ 0.49 for “bb”, then rises to ≈ 0.90 for “WNBA”, fluctuates between ≈ 0.82 and 0.93 across subsequent labels, and ends at ≈ 0.93 for “athletics”. The “random” strategy starts at ≈ 0.66 for “cf”, dips to ≈ 0.51 for “bb”, peaks at ≈ 0.88 for “WNBA”, dips to ≈ 0.72 for “ESPN”, rises to ≈ 0.88 for “NHL”, then to ≈ 0.92 for “FIFA”, peaks again at ≈ 0.93 for “Estadio”, and falls to ≈ 0.87 for “athletics”. The “end” strategy begins at ≈ 0.76 for “cf”, drops to ≈ 0.57 for “bb”, climbs to ≈ 0.89 for “WNBA”, dips to ≈ 0.75 for “ESPN”, rises to ≈ 0.89 for “NHL”, drops to ≈ 0.81 for “FIFA”, peaks at ≈ 0.96 for “Estadio”, and ends at ≈ 0.83 for “athletics”. All three lines show non-monotonic behavior, with significant variation across target labels, and the “end” strategy achieves the highest peak ASR at “Estadio”.
